interest: This file is exceptionally valuable for tracing the origins of postwar East Asian territorial disputes, preserving competing Japanese, Korean, and Soviet claims alongside foundational Japanese Foreign Office studies on outlying islands such as Okinawa, the Kuriles, and Liancourt Rocks. It uniquely pairs operational histories and military government records of Okinawa with an exhaustive, prefecture-by-prefecture SCAP inventory of Japan's prewar cultural, historic, and natural monuments. Furthermore, diplomatic exchanges and legal memoranda illuminate the early, unresolved U.S. deliberations surrounding the definition of Japanese territory and sovereignty prior to the San Francisco Peace Treaty.
overview: This file documents the post–World War II determination of Japan's territorial boundaries, outlying islands, and sovereignty between 1945 and 1949 under Allied occupation. It brings together diplomatic correspondence, legal opinions, and petitions from Japanese civic and prefectural bodies as well as Korean organizations concerning the status of the Ryukyu Islands (Okinawa), the Kurile Islands, Habomai, Shikotan, the Bonin and Volcano Islands, and the Liancourt Rocks. The collection also features extensive Japanese Foreign Office historical and geographical monographs on adjacent islands, U.S. Ryukyus Command military government reports, civil affairs handbooks and operational accounts of the Battle of Okinawa, and an exhaustive SCAP inventory of designated Japanese historic sites, scenic spots, and natural monuments, alongside early surveys of Hiroshima's postwar reconstruction.
